added_models.model: Human colorectal patient-derived xenografts (PDX) in mice

efficacy.model: Human colorectal patient-derived xenografts (PDX) in mice
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via scrape; the colon PDX single-agent tumour-growth-inhibition number sits in Figure 6B, which was not read. The 2023 FDA review names no PDX study, so model_filed is false.
efficacy.note: Fruquintinib, alone and with oxaliplatin, was tested in the colon cancer PDX COL1T0117P4 (Sun 2014); no patient data yet for comparison.
efficacy.short: Colon PDX COL1T0117P4 dosed with fruquintinib
efficacy.quote: Similarly, the enhanced inhibitory effect of fruquintinib with oxaliplatin was seen in the colon cancer PDX model COL1T0117P4
efficacy.judgement: A PDX is a different system from the HT-29/LoVo cell-line xenografts on the crc-xenograft-rodent track (patient tumour, serially passaged, no cell-line adaptation), so it gets its own track.

efficacy.model: Human colorectal patient-derived xenografts (PDX) in mice
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX tumour growth inhibition (fruquintinib alone and with oxaliplatin, figure only) vs placebo-controlled PFS hazard ratio 0.30; not commensurable
efficacy.confidence_note: Pairing made here: Xu 2017 does not cite the PDX. Model side read in full text (scrape); trial side at abstract level, quote verbatim in the abstract.
efficacy.note: The colon PDX predicted fruquintinib activity; the placebo-controlled phase II in refractory mCRC met its PFS primary endpoint (HR 0.30).
efficacy.short: Phase II PFS HR 0.30 vs placebo
efficacy.quote: PFS was significantly improved with fruquintinib plus BSC (4.73 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.86-5.59) versus placebo plus BSC (0.99 months; 95% CI 0.95-1.58); (hazard ratio [HR] 0.30; 95% CI 0.15-0.59; P < 0.001).
efficacy.judgement: Direction only: the PDX experiment was a combination with oxaliplatin and the trial was monotherapy versus placebo, so only the sign of single-agent activity transfers. Apatinib/rivoceranib was also run in CRC PDX (Jia 2018, doi 10.7150/jca.20964, with the cMet inhibitor volitinib) but its CRC patient data are single-arm only, so that drug changes nothing on this track. outcome_tested positive: FRESCO (NCT02314819) and FRESCO-2 (NCT04322539, results 2023-09-14) later confirmed on overall survival.

patient_trials.quote: The median OS was 7.72 versus 5.52 months (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.38-1.34).

added_models.model: Simcyp PBPK model of fruquintinib (CYP3A victim and P-gp/BCRP perpetrator DDI)

dose.model: Simcyp PBPK model of fruquintinib (CYP3A victim and P-gp/BCRP perpetrator DDI)
dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the review does not date the applicant's PBPK report (HUMP-2-B); the clinical DDI study it was fitted on (NCT04557397) was first posted 2020-09-21, so the model was built 2021-2023.
dose.note: Applicant's Simcyp model built to predict fruquintinib exposure under CYP3A modulators and its effect on P-gp/BCRP substrates.
dose.short: PBPK DDI model filed with the NDA
dose.quote: The Applicant conducted PBPK analysis to assess DDI potentials of fruquintinib as a victim when coadministered with CYP3A4 modulators and as an inhibitor when coadministered with P-gp and BCRP transporter substrates.
dose.judgement: In-silico dose model, a separate system from the animal PK/PD track; opener at first public use.

dose.model: Simcyp PBPK model of fruquintinib (CYP3A victim and P-gp/BCRP perpetrator DDI)
dose.magnitude_basis: simulated vs observed fruquintinib AUC ratio in healthy subjects: rifampin 0.34 vs 0.35 (Sim/Obs 0.97), itraconazole 1.18 vs 1.1 (Sim/Obs 1.07); FDA Table 76
dose.population: Healthy subjects in the CYP3A DDI study (NCT04557397); label population is refractory mCRC
dose.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled 217564 Multidiscipline review (Appendix 20.4). NCT04557397 has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, so registry_date is null.
dose.note: FDA: the model, fitted on the itraconazole study and verified on rifampin, reproduced both DDI results and was relied on for the untested efavirenz dosing statement.
dose.short: PBPK reproduced rifampin and itraconazole DDI
dose.quote: The model captured the observed fruquintinib PK changes when coadministered with itraconazole (AUCR was 1.1) and rifampin (AUCR was 0.35), a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and a strong CYP3A4 inducer, respectively.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction, not same: fmCYP3A4 was refined on the itraconazole result and rifampin served as the verification set, both known before the model was finalised. Its one prospective prediction (efavirenz, AUC 68% of baseline) became the label's no-dose-adjustment statement for moderate CYP3A inducers without a clinical study, a regulator reliance on the in-silico model that stays untested in humans, so no fresh entry. The model concerns exposure under co-medication, not the efficacy exposure target; filed under dose as the brief's in-silico dose-choice case and flagged for the checker.
dose.reason: FDA: PBPK captured both clinical DDI results

added_models.model: Patient-derived mCRC spheroids, ex-vivo drug-sensitivity profiling (42-drug panel incl. tivozanib)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived mCRC spheroids, ex-vivo drug-sensitivity profiling (42-drug panel incl. tivozanib)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC13168235, epub 2026-03-19). The anti-VEGFR comparison used 3 patients (ID1, ID5, ID12) whose anti-angiogenic therapy was bevacizumab-based.
efficacy.note: Tivozanib was one of 9 anti-VEGFR compounds screened; the source's stated discordance with clinic was against bevacizumab regimens, not a member drug.
efficacy.short: Spheroids screened with tivozanib; no member-drug patients
efficacy.quote: Sensitivity to anti-EGFR drugs distinguished responsive from resistant patients and revealed candidates for anti-ERBB2 therapy, whereas anti-VEGFR screening failed to recapitulate clinical outcomes.
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not contra: the only patient responses compared were to bevacizumab (anti-VEGF-A antibody, outside the member list) and regorafenib (multikinase, outside the list), so under the do-not-widen rule the member-class track has no admissible comparison. The source itself concludes that non-vascularised 3D models cannot read anti-angiogenic activity and drops VEGFR inhibitors from future panels.

efficacy.population: Colorectal cancer, 22 patients (chip-vs-clinic set); 5 patients for the small-molecule panel
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC13400167, first published 2026-06-17). Apatinib and fruquintinib were dosed on chips from five patients (Figure 6); the one drug-matched patient (P15) received regorafenib.
efficacy.note: Apatinib and fruquintinib were tested on patient chips; the 86% chip-vs-clinic accuracy was for FOLFOX plus bevacizumab, and the one followed patient got regorafenib.
efficacy.short: Chips dosed with apatinib/fruquintinib; patients got bevacizumab
efficacy.quote: This study confirms the effectiveness of this model and verifies the variation in the response of tumoroid-on-a-chip models from different patients to FOLFOX plus bevacizumab.
efficacy.judgement: A separate system from the spheroids: self-assembled tumour vasculature under perfusion is the feature the spheroid paper lacked. Untested for this class because no patient in the study received fruquintinib or apatinib; the clinical concordance claim is for bevacizumab plus FOLFOX and the drug-matched case is regorafenib, both outside the member list.

Rivoceranib/apatinib CRC cell-line xenografts (LoVo vessel normalisation, Acta Pharmacol Sin 2019 doi 10.1038/s41401-018-0058-y; Onco Targets Ther 2020 doi 10.2147/OTT.S266549): same system as crc-xenograft-rodent; rivoceranib CRC patient data are single-arm only
Eskens 2011 DCE-MRI/sVEGFR-2 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0411): patient-side readout for the existing track's engagement cell (checker correction), not a model system

KDR rs2071559 pharmacogenetics in 108 apatinib-treated mCRC patients (Int J Gen Med 2021, doi 10.2147/ijgm.s300968): retrospective genotype-outcome association inside the treated cohort, no model prediction made before the patient result; not a human_genetic model of the class
Fruquintinib population PK (J Clin Pharmacol 2025, doi 10.1002/jcph.70001) and FDA exposure-response analyses: descriptive fits of patient data, not predictions compared with patients

Fruquintinib P-gp/BCRP PBPK (perpetrator arm, FDA 2023; clinical study NCT05368805, Clin Transl Sci 2025 doi 10.1111/cts.70408): same Simcyp system as the added track; the review states consistency but only the CYP3A victim arm was quotable with numbers
Fruquintinib + TAS-102 CRC and gastric xenografts (BMC Cancer 2026, doi 10.1186/s12885-026-16153-5): cell-line xenografts, same system as crc-xenograft-rodent; FRUQUITAS phase III not read out
Patient-derived tumour-like cell clusters for CRC chemosensitivity (Transl Oncol 2025, doi 10.1016/j.tranon.2025.102518): chemotherapy only, no VEGFR inhibitor tested
Sun 2014 mouse lung VEGF-induced pVEGFR2 PD model: already folded into the draft's crc-xenograft-rodent engagement and dose entries

Zebrafish xenografts, human challenge models, organoids with a member drug compared to that patient's response, and cross-indication (RCC to CRC) use of tivozanib: no source found for member drugs in CRC; BATON-CRC is already in the draft's patient_trials
